final_summary:
Space Fractions has been implemented as a local desktop application using Python 3 and Tkinter. It includes:

- Intro screen with animation, main menu, play flow, help, score view, and admin-only question editor
- Multiple fraction questions, answer validation with feedback, score updates, pause/resume, and final score screen
- Clear separation between UI, game logic, and data management so core behavior is testable without GUI automation
- Tests verifying question loading, answer validation, scoring, progression, and state transitions

How to run
- Prerequisite: Python 3.9+ with Tkinter available
- Optional: create/activate a virtualenv
- Install test dependency: pip install -r requirements.txt
- Launch the desktop game: python main.py
- Run tests: pytest -q

Key adaptation notes
- The source architecture specifies microservices (GameComponent, QuestionComponent, UserComponent), web UI, cloud deployment, OpenAPI/proto, PostgreSQL/Redis, and OAuth2. To satisfy the explicit desktop constraint, these are mapped to:
  - Local modules: core/game.py, core/question.py, core/user.py; services/question_service.py and user_service.py; ui/* screens
  - Local JSON data instead of databases
  - Local function interfaces instead of REST/gRPC
  - Simple local role gate for admin (demo password “admin”) instead of OAuth2
- Observability, Kubernetes, and CI/CD are deferred as non-applicable to a single-user desktop application. Functional intent is preserved.

Use-case coverage
- Play Game: space_fractions/ui/game_view.py + space_fractions/core/game.py
- View Score: space_fractions/ui/score_view.py + services/user_service.py (last_score.json)
- View Help: space_fractions/ui/help_view.py
- Update Questions (Admin): space_fractions/ui/admin_view.py + services/question_service.py (questions.json)

Verification
- Tests executed and passed:
  - /Users/macbookpro/Work/Projects/CodeAgentArc/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q

Assumptions and warnings
- Introductory “movie” is an animated text effect due to no media assets
- Admin authentication is demonstrative (password “admin”)
- Local JSON storage replaces PostgreSQL/Redis and is not multi-user durable
- Web/microservice deployment guidance was mapped to a local desktop runtime due to the explicit task constraint

You can start the app with: python main.py
Use the Admin option in the main menu to edit questions after logging in as admin with password “admin”.

completion.summary:
Created Space Fractions as a fully local desktop application using Python 3 and Tkinter. Implemented the GameComponent, QuestionComponent, and UserComponent as Python modules mapping the microservice responsibilities to in-process components. Delivered a playable GUI with intro screen, main menu, play flow for fraction questions, answer validation and feedback, visible score updates, pause/resume, progression to a final score screen, help/instructions, and an admin-only question editor. Replaced cloud/web/microservice deployment, REST/gRPC, OAuth2, and DB/Redis with local module boundaries and JSON files while preserving functional intent. Provided non-GUI domain tests that exercise question selection, answer validation, scoring, progression, and state transitions. Added README with assumptions, conflicts, and adaptation decisions. Entry point is python main.py; tests via pytest.

Key mappings and decisions
- Source facts: Microservices style with GameComponent, QuestionComponent, UserComponent; Use cases Play Game, View Score, View Help, Update Questions; states Playing, Paused, GameOver. Cloud and API delivery. These are preserved as module responsibilities and realized use cases in the desktop UI.
- Adaptation: No web server/browser; APIs mapped to Python function interfaces; PostgreSQL/Redis mapped to local JSON storage; OAuth2 mapped to demo local admin password gate; Kubernetes/observability deferred as not applicable to local desktop.
- Implementation choices: Retry-until-correct question progression (only advance when correct) to align with domain tests; score +1 per correct answer; initial sample questions included; simple animated intro due to absent media assets.
- Ambiguities/conflicts: Concurrency and cloud scalability assumptions (A1: 1000 concurrent users) do not apply locally; introductory “movie” implemented as animated text; admin auth is demonstrative only. All such deviations are documented in README.

Use-case to code mapping
- Play Game: space_fractions/ui/game_view.py + space_fractions/core/game.py
- View Score: space_fractions/ui/score_view.py + services/user_service.py (last_score.json)
- View Help: space_fractions/ui/help_view.py
- Update Questions: space_fractions/ui/admin_view.py + services/question_service.py (questions.json)

Repository summary
- main.py (launches GUI). Space-separated screens: Intro, Menu, Play, Help, Score, Admin Editor.
- Core logic separated from UI for testability. Data folder with starter questions.
- requirements.txt with pytest, .gitignore, and README.

Verification
- Installed test dependency and executed pytest; domain tests cover validation, scoring, progression, and state transitions. All tests passed.
assumptions: Local single-user desktop runtime replaces cloud deployment and microservices networking.
Introductory movie is represented as a lightweight animation due to no assets.
Admin authentication is represented by a fixed demo password 'admin' for gating Update Questions.
Progression requires correct answer to advance (non-specified in source, chosen to satisfy domain tests and pedagogy).
warnings: Security model is demonstrative and not production-grade; do not reuse fixed password.
Local JSON storage is not durable or multi-user-safe compared to the source’s PostgreSQL/Redis.
Observability, CI/CD, and Kubernetes aspects from the source are intentionally deferred as out of scope for a single desktop app.
